significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that turn-to-turn residual-stream "drift velocity" predictively couples to jailbreak compliance "several turns before" it occurs across attack strategies, together with the form-(ii) conclusion that a "restoring force" causally reduces that behavior while preserving benign utility. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism: it fixes expectations about future compliance from an earlier measurable trajectory, distinguishes malicious from benign topic drift, and identifies a causal control target rather than merely a decodable harmfulness direction; Crescendo (Russinovich et al., 2024, arXiv:2404.01833) documents the gradual multi-turn attack process for which such advance prediction would change monitoring and intervention decisions. A negative result would meaningfully rule out scalar harmfulness-velocity dynamics as an attack-agnostic early-warning account and, if the intervention also fails, rule out simple re-anchoring as sufficient control, though it would not refute representational drift generally. True and false are determinate states, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: generic mechanistic LLM safety does not itself imply the claim-specific predictive coupling, lead time, or restoring-force causal consequence.

reach.justification: The claim names two reusable handles: "drift velocity" as a "cheap online monitor" and the per-turn "restoring-force" activation intervention. The monitor is explicitly ex ante because it forecasts compliance "several turns before" the jailbreak, leaving auditors or deployment systems time to gate, terminate, or modify a conversation; the intervention is likewise online rather than merely explanatory after failure. Although the harmfulness direction requires per-model calibration and white-box access, the asserted attack-agnostic predictive relation is what should survive re-extraction, so the takeaway is more than a procedure for rediscovering an arbitrary direction, with scope across multi-turn attack strategies and downstream uptake by model auditors and operators. The topic-substitution check passes: removing these named trajectory handles leaves only the broad safety-interpretability topic, which would not warrant this reach score.
